title: CODA: Temporal Domain Generalization via Concept Drift Simulator

problem.claim: Real-world machine learning models often suffer performance issues under data distribution shifts, motivating temporal domain generalization for maintaining future performance under concept drift.

gap.claim: Existing model-centric training strategies may require extensive data-model interaction to train appropriately for distribution shifts.

contributions.claim: The CODA framework uses a predicted feature correlation matrix to simulate future data for model training.
CODA uses feature correlations to represent data characteristics at each time point and trigger future data generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CODA-generated training data effectively achieves temporal domain generalization across different model architectures.
The authors report great transferability across different model architectures.

narrative_sequence.summary: Distribution shifts can impair real-world machine learning performance.
Temporal domain generalization seeks to preserve future performance under concept drift.
Existing model-centric approaches may require extensive interaction between data and model.
CODA generates future training data using a predicted feature correlation matrix, and the authors report effective temporal domain generalization across model architectures.

source_observation.claim: Generating future-domain data is presented as a way to bypass cumbersome data-model interaction during training for distribution shifts.

interpretation.claim: A data-centric simulation strategy may reduce reliance on repeatedly adapting the model to shifted data.

application.claim: For temporal shift problems, consider modeling evolving data characteristics and generating future-domain training inputs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when simulated future data may fail to represent actual future distributions.
